prompt: [brisk, curious, restrained tension] Imagine firing liquid at a criminal—and watching it turn into a web that CATCHES them. [confident, conversational] Scientists have taken the first step toward that. [brisk, clear] They start with silk from moth cocoons and dissolve it into a liquid. [flowing, explanatory] As it shoots through a special nozzle, a surrounding layer of acetone triggers the silk to harden. [crisp] A sticky fiber forms in midair. It hits the metal and attaches. [leaning in, building] Then you pull—and the blade LIFTS out of the sand. [impressed, controlled] In lab tests, these fibers lifted over EIGHTY times their own weight. [quietly knowing] The beginnings of a real web shooter… made from moth silk.
note_on_prompt: Bracketed tags are delivery directions (not spoken); capitals are emphasis. The spoken words are exactly the locked narration (production/NARRATION_APPROVED.txt).

takes.verdict: Verbatim. Whisper base.en differs only in spelling ("mid-air", "80"); zipformer only in spelling/compounding ("fibre", "labtests", "webshooter") and one recogniser miss ("acidone" for acetone). The small Vosk and PocketSphinx models mishear "moth cocoons" ("moscow coons" / "all the cruise") and "lifts" ("lives"); the two stronger models hear both correctly.
